stem: When teaching recipient hand-hygiene practices after transplantation, which timing aligns with standard infection-prevention references?

options.text: Wash hands after using the bathroom
Hand-washing is needed only before the first meal of the day
Soap and water are never needed after bathroom use if gel is available
Bathroom hand-washing applies only to pediatric recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipient hand-hygiene teaching includes washing hands after using the bathroom, along with washing before preparing or eating meals and after contact with secretions or animals.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hand-washing is needed at multiple times throughout the day, not only before the first meal.
rationale_incorrect.C: Soap and water remain important when hands are soiled; gel supplements but does not replace appropriate washing.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant hand-hygiene guidance applies to all recipients, not pediatric recipients alone.

stem: A donor family asks what general recipient information the OPO may share without recipient permission. Which example aligns with standard donor–recipient confidentiality references?

options.text: Recipient age described in decades, general status of health, and gender
Recipient full name, address, and telephone number
Recipient employment history and income details
Recipient social security number and insurance policy numbers

explanation.rationale_correct: The OPO may provide general recipient status information to the donor family without recipient permission, including age described in decades, general status of health, and gender.

rationale_incorrect.B: Identifying information such as full name and contact details is not among the general information that may be shared without permission.
rationale_incorrect.C: Employment and income details are not listed as permissible general information for donor families.
rationale_incorrect.D: Social security and insurance identifiers are not described as general information shareable without recipient permission.

stem: When reinforcing home infection-prevention teaching for a recipient with household pets, which hand-hygiene step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Wash hands after contact with animals
Hand-washing after animal contact is unnecessary if pets are indoor only
Only veterinary staff need hand hygiene after animal contact
Animal contact requires stopping all immunosuppression temporarily

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipient hand-hygiene teaching includes washing hands after contact with animals, along with other high-risk contacts such as soil, plants, and secretions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hand-washing after animal contact is specifically recommended regardless of whether pets remain indoors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Recipients themselves should practice hand hygiene after animal contact rather than delegating it to veterinary staff alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression continues as prescribed; infection prevention emphasizes hygiene rather than stopping therapy.

stem: A coordinator is updating hand-hygiene and donor-confidentiality teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should wash hands after using the bathroom.
Recipients should wash hands after contact with animals.
The OPO may share recipient age described in decades with the donor family without recipient permission.
Recipient identifying information may always be shared freely with donor families without restriction.

explanation.rationale_correct: Bathroom and animal-contact hand hygiene and sharing general recipient age information without permission are supported. Statement IV is false because only limited general information may be shared without recipient permission.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—the OPO may share general age-decade information without recipient permission.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because unrestricted sharing of identifying information is not permitted.
